A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UI2CodeN research and contain 27 readable pages, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H. Textual and visual inspection supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original UI drafting, polishing, and editing experiments, human evaluations, ablations, and evaluator-validation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark results, human evaluations, ablations, and evaluator-validation studies, including Table 1 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The 9B model, three-stage training pipeline, RVPO reward construction, Algorithm 1, GRPO update, and iterative drafting/polishing/editing procedures are unchanged. Correcting VRPO to RVPO standardizes naming without changing the method.

E1.justification: Training corpora and evaluated tasks remain unchanged, including Design2Code/HARD, Flame, Web2Code, UI2Code-Real, synthetic/real polishing, UIEdit-Bench, and WebCode2M-Long. Moving appendix experiments into the main text does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained across corresponding experiments. DCGen and ScreenCoder move from v3 Table 15 to v4 Table 4; the specialized WebSight VLM-7B, Design2Code-18B, and UICopilot comparisons also remain. Capitalization changes do not identify new baselines.

E3.justification: The reported Design2Code-HARD agent comparison drops DINO accuracy, retaining VLM-judge accuracy, latency, and token cost in v4 Table 4. Other evaluation settings, sample sizes, judge protocols, and training budgets remain unchanged. This narrows reported metric coverage without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Reward-design, real-data, training-stage, absolute-positioning, evaluator-robustness, and polishing-oscillation analyses are retained. The training-stage and reward-hacking studies move from v3 Appendices G and A.4 into v4 Sections 4.5 and 4.3 with the same evidence. The demonstration cases also match.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent generation-and-evaluation runs with means and standard deviations in Appendix F.3, renumbered from Table 10 to Table 12. Human-annotation counts, agreement statistics, correlations, effect sizes, and uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: v4 omits the Design2Code-HARD DINO entries from v3 Table 15: DCGen 69.6, ScreenCoder 85.7, and UI2CodeN-RL 86.1. Their VLM accuracies and resource costs remain unchanged, as do other matched quantitative results. The shortened training-stage discussion also omits v3's qualitative observation that CPT-only models often fail instruction or formatting constraints.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, objectives, and Equations 1–19 are retained. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised; the additional efficiency paragraph is explanatory prose.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: interactive visual optimization, relative-preference RVPO, and a compact 9B model claiming strong performance across drafting, polishing, and editing. The rewritten conclusion and corrected acronym do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly identifies misuse through website cloning or reproduction of protected designs. Its shortened experimental discussions remove detailed explanations connecting reward design to shortcut resistance and agent-pipeline failures to detection/OCR error propagation, while retaining the principal interpretations.

D1.justification: Section 2.3 newly states that independent post-hoc pairwise comparisons can be parallelized across workers, adding limited implementation guidance without documenting an actual configuration change. Hyperparameters, verifier prompts, access information, and the Table 20 timing breakdown—including the 2.2% comparison cost—were already present.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the cited-work set are unchanged. The relocated agent-system comparison retains the existing positioning of UI2CodeN as a simpler, lower-cost alternative; no new prior-work relationship or novelty claim is introduced.

P1.justification: v4 moves and condenses several appendix discussions into the main text, adds conflict-of-interest and funding disclosures, expands the efficiency explanation, and revises the conclusion. It also standardizes RVPO and benchmark terminology and shortens running headers. These are localized edits rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Existing tables and figures are repositioned as the text reflows. The agent comparison becomes a narrower main-text table without its DINO column, and the relocated training-stage table gains an explicit Gain heading. Figure content and appendix demonstration images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves transparency through explicit conflict-of-interest and funding disclosures, corrects inconsistent RVPO naming, and makes existing supporting experiments easier to find in the main text. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of DINO comparison results and explanatory detail. The method, central empirical evidence, and principal conclusions remain unchanged.
